---
title: "Capturing from the web"
subtitle: "One click on any paper page saves it — with its PDF — into FluxLib"
---

You are reading a paper in your browser. One click puts it in your library: the reference, and
the PDF, without a download folder detour or a copy-pasted DOI.

# Setting it up

In [Library](../modes/library.qmd), at the bottom of the pane, the **Web capture** row shows
whether capture is connected. Click **Set up…** and follow the two lines for your browser:

- **Firefox** — one button, **Install for Firefox**. Firefox asks you to confirm, and that's it.
- **Chrome, Edge or Brave** — **Show me the folder** opens the extension folder, **Copy address**
  gives you `chrome://extensions` to paste in a new tab, then turn on *Developer mode* and
  choose **Load unpacked**.

::: {.callout-note}
Flux can't open `chrome://extensions` or `about:addons` for you — browsers refuse navigation to
those from outside, deliberately. That's why the panel opens the folder and hands you the
address to paste rather than pretending to do it in one click.
:::

The status dot turns green the moment your first capture arrives, so you never have to wonder
whether it took.

# Using it

Open a paper and click the **Flux** button in your browser's toolbar. It works on the article
page **and** on a PDF you already have open. The badge tells you what happened:

| Badge | What happened |
|---|---|
| A number, green | That many files captured — the article plus its supplementary files. |
| `1`, amber | No PDF was reachable, so the paper's details were captured. Flux still adds the reference; it just won't have the PDF yet. |
| `!`, red | Nothing was captured. **Hover the button** — the tooltip says why. |

Supplementary files come with the article in the same click: SI PDFs, spreadsheets, videos.
Each is filed against the paper once Flux has identified it, so a supplement for a paper you
don't have yet simply waits until the paper arrives.

Captures land in a **`flux/` subfolder** of your downloads folder, named `flux-…`, and Flux
removes them as it files them. **Flux doesn't need to be open** — anything captured while it's closed is swept up when
you next start it, and again whenever you switch back to the Flux window. Nothing is lost, and nothing else in your downloads folder is touched: Flux
only ever looks at files it wrote itself.

A captured PDF goes through the same identification as the
[drop folder](../modes/library.qmd#getting-papers-in) — Flux reads the document's own content
(embedded DOI, then the DOI printed on page 1, then its reference list, then a title search) to
find the right reference. It attaches to a paper you already have, or adds the reference if it's
new.

# Why capture from the browser

Flux can already fetch open-access PDFs on its own, and paywalled ones through your
[library proxy](../modes/library.qmd). But some publishers sit behind anti-bot systems —
Cloudflare and PerimeterX — that refuse automated browsers outright, no matter how the request
is dressed up. Those papers are simply unreachable to Flux.

Your browser is not an automated browser. It's you: already signed in, already past the
paywall, already holding the session. The extension captures the PDF *from inside your own
session*, which is why it reaches papers Flux cannot fetch by itself. It's the most capable
acquisition route in the app, and it costs one click.

# Browser support

| Browser | |
|---|---|
| **Firefox** | Fully supported, installed from the signed add-on. |
| **Chrome, Edge, Brave** | Fully supported, loaded from the extension folder. |
| **Safari** | Not supported — Safari uses a different extension format. Save the PDF yourself and drop it into FluxLib's `pdfs_to_assign` folder. |

# If nothing happens

- **Hover the toolbar button.** The tooltip carries the reason the last capture failed,
  including the browser's own error code when a publisher refused the download.
- **Check the address bar** for a blocked-download icon, and allow it.
- **Some publishers refuse the PDF but not the page.** You get the amber badge and the
  reference still arrives — just without its PDF. Flux can often fetch that separately with
  **Get PDFs**.
- **Internal pages can't be captured** (`about:`, `chrome://`, the extensions page itself) —
  browsers don't allow it.

# Where things land

| | |
|---|---|
| Captured files | `<downloads>/flux/`, named `flux-…` (removed as Flux files them) |
| Captured PDFs, once filed | `FluxLib/pdfs_to_assign/`, then `FluxLib/items/<citekey>/paper.pdf` |
| Captured supplements | `FluxLib/items/<citekey>/supplements/` (they wait, staged, until the article has been identified) |
| PDFs that couldn't be identified | `FluxLib/pdfs_to_assign/_unresolved/`, with a note saying why |

Nothing is ever guessed: a PDF Flux can't identify with confidence is set aside rather than
attached to the wrong paper.
